# TextField

Text field — a labeled single-line field on `_Field`, 40 high and 32 when `spacing="compact"`. Label, field and caption: the caption shows a message (or standing help) on the left and, when `maxLength` is set, a count on the right. `elemBeforeInput` and `elemAfterInput` fill the slots on either side of the control; a string is a text affix. With `appearance="subtle"`, the field reads as plain text until it is hovered or edited, and saves on blur or Enter through `onSave`. `type="number"` adds steppers after the control. Empty is not 0: an empty field stays empty, and stepping from it starts at 0 (or the nearest bound). A typed value outside `min`/`max` is clamped when the field loses focus, not while it is typed. The field is a text input, so the scroll wheel never changes the value.

Also asked as: search box, single-line, text box.

**Import:** `import { TextField } from '@/components';`

## Usage

Use a Text field for single-line text entry: names, emails, search boxes and
numbers. It owns its label, its validation state and its message, which makes it
the right home for an error rather than a Section message at the top of the form.

Use a [Text area](?path=/docs/components-forms-and-inputs-text-area--docs) for several lines, a
Select for a value chosen from a list, and a Date picker for dates.

## Motion

TextField reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Border color changes on focus and error. An error message makes room, then fades in; it fades, then the room closes, once the field is fixed. |

## Best practices

### Name the field. {#name-the-field}

The label says what the field is, not what to do.

Do: The label names the field.
Don't: An instruction where the name should be reads badly in a list of fields.

### Put one element on each side, at most. {#put-one-element-on-each-side-at-most}

A leading icon or a trailing action, not both crowding the text.

Do: One element before the text.
Don't: Elements on both sides squeeze the value.

### Hint at the answer, not the control. {#hint-at-the-answer-not-the-control}

A placeholder shows what a good answer looks like.

Do: Hint shows the format.
Don't: Hint describes the control.

### Show an error on the field itself. {#show-an-error-on-the-field-itself}

The field carries the invalid state.

Do: The field shows the invalid state.
Don't: A default field gives no sign of the problem.

### Say what to do about an error. {#say-what-to-do-about-an-error}

Do: Say what to do about the error, in the field's own caption.
Don't: A fact that there is an error, with no way forward.

### Keep slots to decoration. {#keep-slots-to-decoration}

A string is a text affix; an icon is hidden from assistive technology. Anything the reader must know belongs in the label or the message, not in the glyph. Do not nest interactive elements in a slot, other than the Button the field is built for: a control with its own focus is announced apart from the field.

### Let the message follow the state. {#let-the-message-follow-the-state}

`errorMessage` shows with `isInvalid`; `warningMessage` and `successMessage` show on their own; otherwise `caption` shows. `maxLength` adds a count on the right beside any of them. A warning accepts the value: use it when the entry is allowed but worth a second look, and `isInvalid` only when the form cannot go on.

### Set `autoComplete` on every field the browser can fill. {#set-autocomplete-on-every-field-the-browser-can-fill}

Login email is `email`, the password is `current-password`, and an access code is `one-time-code`.

### Use subtle for editing in place. {#use-subtle-for-editing-in-place}

`appearance="subtle"` is for record and profile pages, never in a form someone fills from top to bottom. Pass `onSave`.

### Pick the spacing by the row it sits in. {#pick-the-spacing-by-the-row-it-sits-in}

Use `default` in forms and `compact` in toolbars, filter bars and table rows.

### Use `type="number"` for quantities you step. {#use-type-number-for-quantities-you-step}

Such as seats. For an ID, a phone number or a ZIP code, use `type="text"` with `inputMode`.

### Read-only is not disabled. {#read-only-is-not-disabled}

`isReadOnly` shows a value someone could change but this person cannot right now: it stays in the tab order at full contrast, can be selected and copied, takes the neutral fill, has no hover and says `aria-readonly`. Say why in the caption. `isDisabled` is for a field that does not apply yet, and takes it out of the tab order. Never swap one for the other, and never clip a read-only value. Content nobody can edit is plain text, not a field.

Do: Read-only keeps the value readable, and the caption says why.
Don't: Disabled fades a value people need to read.

## Accessibility

- **The label is associated whether you pass `id` or not.** One id is derived
  once and used for both the label's `htmlFor` and the input.
- **`isLabelHidden` hides the label, it does not remove it.** The label is
  rendered either way and clipped out of sight. A field that has a `label` has an
  accessible name whether or not you show it. If the visible label is rendered
  by the caller instead, point it at the input with `htmlFor`; if there is no
  text anywhere, pass `aria-label`.
- **`isRequired` shows an asterisk and sets `aria-required`.** The asterisk is
  hidden from assistive technology. The form explains it once, in a legend above
  the fields.
- **An error is announced.** The message gets an id, the input points at it with
  `aria-describedby`, and `isInvalid` sets `aria-invalid` and renders the message
  with `role="alert"`. A warning, a success message and standing help are
  described without being announced. Your own `aria-describedby` is kept and the
  message id is appended.
- **Focus is a ring**, with no change of fill, so it reads in Light, Dark and
  More contrast.
- **The number field is a text input**, so the scroll wheel never changes the
  value. The steppers are named for the field they change: "Decrease Seats" and "Increase Seats".

## Parts

1. **Label.** Names the field. A required marker and an info tooltip sit beside it.
2. **Before.** An icon, a text affix or a Button before the control.
3. **Control.** The native input.
4. **After.** An icon, a text affix, a Button or the number steppers.
5. **Caption.** A message on the left and, with `maxLength`, a count on the right.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The input fill with a `--border-default` input edge; the placeholder until there is text. |
| Hovered | The edge turns `--ds-border-focused`. A subtle field takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered edge holds while the pointer is down. |
| Focused | A `--focus-ring-width` ring in `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` off the box. No fill changes. |
| Disabled | The whole field fades to `--ds-opacity-disabled` and leaves the tab order. |
| Invalid | The edge takes `--ds-border-danger` and the message `--ds-text-danger`. |
| Warning, success | The edge takes `--ds-border-warning` or `--ds-border-success`, with the message in the matching text color. |
| Read-only | The `--ds-background-neutral` fill, full contrast, no hover. The value can be read, selected and copied; number steppers are not drawn. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Box | `--ds-background-input` fill, `--border-default` edge in `--ds-border-input`. |
| Height | 40: `--height-250`. Compact 32: `--item-height-md`. |
| Radius | 10: `--radius-0625`. Compact 8: `--radius-control-md`. |
| Side padding | `--pad-x-md`; a Button in a slot sits `--pad-x-xs` from the edge. |
| Slot button | `--item-height-md` in the 40 field, `--item-height-sm` in the 32 field. |
| Slots | `--ds-text-subtle`, `--stack-sm` apart; `--space-0625` between slot and control. |
| Text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`; placeholder `--ds-text-subtlest`. |
| Label and caption | `--body-small`; label `--ds-text`, caption `--ds-text-subtle`; the count `--ds-text-subtle`, over the limit `--ds-text-danger`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the field with a short noun: "Email address". | An instruction where the name belongs: "Enter your email address here". |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation on labels. | Title case, or a period after the label. |
| Say what to do about an error: "Enter a 10-digit number." | "Invalid" or "Error". |
| Keep helper text to one short line. | Paragraphs in the caption. Link to help instead. |
| Put the unit in an affix: "kg". | The unit in the label or the value. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Id of the input, which the label points at. A generated id is used when omitted. |
| `name` | string | — | Form key of the input. Number steppers also report it in the `onChange` event. |
| `label` | node | — | Visible label above the field. A string label also names the number steppers, as "Increase" and "Decrease" followed by the label. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Shows an asterisk and sets `aria-required`. Explain the asterisk once, in the form's legend. |
| `isLabelHidden` | bool | `false` | Hides the label visually. It is still rendered and still names the input. |
| `info` | node | — | Text for an info tooltip beside the label. |
| `caption` | node | — | Standing help under the field. A message takes its place. |
| `placeholder` | string | — | Hint text shown while the input is empty. It does not replace a label. |
| `value` | string or number | — | With `type="number"`, empty (`''` or `null`) stays empty; it is never read as 0. |
| `defaultValue` | string or number | — | Starting value of an uncontrolled field. Use `value` to control it instead. |
| `inputRef` | func or shape or any | — | Ref to the underlying `<input>`, as a callback or a ref object. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` is 40; `compact` is 32. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'standard'` | `subtle` is borderless until hovered or edited, for editing in place. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Disables the input and its number steppers and dims the field. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | With `type="number"`, also hides the steppers; the value can be read and copied. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | Draws the error border and sets `aria-invalid`; `errorMessage` says why. |
| `errorMessage` | node | — | Shown in the caption in place of `caption` when `isInvalid` is true. |
| `warningMessage` | node | — | Draws the warning border. Does not set `aria-invalid`: the value is accepted. |
| `successMessage` | node | — | Draws the confirmation border. |
| `elemBeforeInput` | node | — | Before the control. A string is a text affix; a node is rendered as given. |
| `elemAfterInput` | node | — | After the control. A string is a text affix; a node is rendered as given. |
| `type` | string | `'text'` | `number` shows steppers and holds the value as text. |
| `maxLength` | number | — | Limits the length and shows a count on the right of the caption. |
| `min` | number | — | `type="number"`: lower bound. A typed value below it is raised to it when the field loses focus. |
| `max` | number | — | `type="number"`: upper bound. A typed value above it is lowered to it when the field loses focus. |
| `step` | number | `1` | `type="number"`: how much a stepper changes the value. |
| `onSave` | func | — | Subtle only: called on blur or Enter with the new value. Throw or reject to keep the field open in `invalid`. |
| `autoComplete` | string | — | Browser autofill token, e.g. `email`, `current-password`, `one-time-code`. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the outer field wrapper, beside `plus-text-field`. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the outer field wrapper. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Called on every edit with the change event. Stepper presses and clamping call it with `{ target: { name, value, type: "number" } }`, the value as text. |
| `onFocus` | func | — | Called with the focus event when the input gains focus. |
| `onBlur` | func | — | Called with the blur event when the input loses focus. A number field is clamped to `min` and `max` first. |
| `onKeyDown` | func | — | Called with the keydown event before the field handles it. Call `event.preventDefault()` to skip a subtle field's own key handling. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |

## Variants

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

**`appearance`** — `standard` · `subtle`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.
